title: Library
intro: Writing and recordings on SHRDLU, from 1971 onward: articles, books, chapters, theses, news items, web pages, talks and films. A copy is held here where the work has an open licence or is in the public domain; otherwise the entry links to where it is published. The list is still growing.

items.title: Procedures as a Representation for Data in a Computer Program for Understanding Natural Language
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, AI-TR-235 (MIT PhD thesis). Primary work by Winograd. The thesis describes the program, its PROGRAMMAR grammar, semantic analysis and Micro-Planner deductive system. SHRDLU: Throughout. Read through the Internet Archive full-text index of the DTIC copy AD0721399, where the program is named as the robot object :SHRDLU; DSpace page returned 200 but is a script shell. Free to read at https://archive.org/details/DTIC_AD0721399

items.title: Understanding Natural Language
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: New York: Academic Press; Edinburgh: Edinburgh University Press. Primary work by Winograd. The book form of the thesis, with the dialogue of section 1.3 and the program description. SHRDLU: Throughout; Internet Archive lending copy, full-text index shows assertions naming :SHRDLU in the Planner section on the data base.

items.title: A Procedural Model of Language Understanding
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Schank, Roger C. and Colby, Kenneth Mark (eds), Computer Models of Thought and Language. San Francisco: W. H. Freeman, chapter 4, pp. 152-186. Primary work by Winograd. A shorter account of the procedural model of the 1972 program. The name SHRDLU does not occur in the indexed text of the volume. SHRDLU: Chapter 4, table of contents p. 152. The Internet Archive index finds no SHRDLU anywhere in this volume; the chapter describes the system without that name and refers to Winograd (1972) for the grammar.

items.title: Formalisation of discourse production
items.author: Davey, Anthony
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Davey treats SHRDLU as a theory of language rather than a data-retrieval system, takes issue with Winograd's rule that 'it' and 'them' are restricted to the last utterance, and discusses its handling of tense, aspect, partial utterances and systemic grammar. SHRDLU: Section 3 survey of earlier programs, printed pp. 52-68, PDF pp. 66-82, including 'Pronouns in Winograd's system' (printed p. 59) and 'Systemic grammar in SHRDLU' (printed p. 65).

items.title: Programming a dialogue teaching situation
items.author: Stansfield, James L.
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Stansfield takes Winograd's procedural representation as one of two paradigms for his teaching program and examines how SHRDLU builds noun-group meanings in PLANNER and orders patterns by weights. SHRDLU: Printed pp. 19-31, PDF pp. 28-40. Title page reads 1974 (OCR '1274'); the repository record gives 1975.

items.title: Five Lectures on Artificial Intelligence
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Memo AIM-246; Stanford Computer Science Department report STAN-CS-74-459. Primary work by Winograd. MIT AI Memo 323 is not this work: the memo of that number at bitsavers is Horn, Orienting Silicon Integrated Circuit Chips for Lead Bonding (January 1975). SHRDLU: Lecture 2 is headed "SHRDLU: A System for Dialog"; Lecture 1 also introduces the program. Read through the IA full-text index of DTIC ADA000085.

items.title: A Report on the Tutorial on Computational Semantics, Institute for Semantics and Cognitive Studies, Villa Heleneum, Lugano-Castagnola, March 17-22, 1975
items.author: Hanon, Suzanne; Koch, Gregers; Søndergaard, Georg
items.note: In: American Journal of Computational Linguistics, Microfiche 17, 47-. Reports Wilks's survey at the Lugano tutorial: SHRDLU is a first-generation system with a grammar of small subprograms, top-down depth-first parsing and semantic specialists, and Woods and Winograd argue their systems are essentially equivalent. SHRDLU: printed pp. 49-50, PDF pp. 3-4.
items.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 (ACL Anthology statement for materials prior to 2016)

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Linguistics: A Brief History of a One-Way Relationship
items.author: Rosenberg, Richard S.
items.note: In: Paper presented at the First Annual Conference of the Berkeley Linguistics Society, February 1975; ERIC ED108511, 15 pp. Treats the removal of sharp divisions between syntax, semantics, inference and context as Winograd's contribution, describes the simulated table of blocks and the commands, questions and declaratives the system takes, and names Halliday's systemic grammar among its linguistic sources. SHRDLU: PDF p. 8 (Winograd section), abstract PDF p. 1. Free to read at https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED108511.pdf

items.title: Parsing English. Course Notes for a Tutorial on Computational Semantics, March 17-22, 1975
items.author: Wilks, Yorick
items.note: In: Institute for Semantic and Cognitive Studies, Castagnola, Switzerland; ERIC ED112684, 68 pp. Describes the dialogue, grammar and PLANNER code, then argues that as regards its semantics the system is about organising goals and subgoals for manipulating physical objects and not about a natural language; compares it with Simmons, Schank, Colby and Wilks. SHRDLU: Section 2, 'Winograd's understanding system', PDF pp. 15-24; abstract PDF p. 1. OCR renders the name in places as SHRKLU. Free to read at https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED112684.pdf

items.title: Computer Modelling of English Grammar
items.author: Ritchie, Graeme D.
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Reviews Winograd's PROGRAMMAR, the use of Halliday's features and semantic specialists, then compares the author's MCHINE program with SHRDLU on storage, sentence times and conversational ability. It describes computational grammar as an attempt to clean up ideas in SHRDLU and LSNLIS. SHRDLU: Section II.9, 'The SHRDLU System (Winograd)', printed pp. 62-64, PDF pp. 72-74; performance comparison in Section VI.5, printed pp. 360-363, PDF pp. 370-373; further comparisons throughout, 41 hits.

items.title: L'informatique juridique : en progression vers un processus d'intelligence artificielle
items.author: Goulet, Jean
items.note: In: Les Cahiers de droit 21(3), 1980. Snippets show the article takes up JUDITH, TAXMAN and SHRDLU as inhabited universes, and promises a later engagement with Shrdlu when defining the parameters of a world like ours. English gloss: Legal informatics: progressing toward a process of artificial intelligence. SHRDLU: Persée search snippets of the Érudit copy; article text on erudit.org is behind a bot check, so the full passage was not read. Footnote 133 names SHRDLU 'la créature de Winograd'.

items.title: What Does it Mean to Understand Language?
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Cognitive Science 4(3): 209-241. Primary work by Winograd. Winograd reviews the assumptions behind SHRDLU and describes the program as a computer program for natural language understanding before turning to the question of background. SHRDLU: Section headed "Up through SHRDLU" and following subsection "SHRDLU" (IA index of the 1981 reprint and of the 1985 reprint). Wiley refused the PDF to curl (403); no copy downloaded. OpenAlex lists the PDF as bronze open access. Free to read at https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1207/s15516709cog0403_1

items.title: What Does it Mean to Understand Language?
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Norman, Donald A. (ed.), Perspectives on Cognitive Science. Norwood, NJ: Ablex. Primary work by Winograd. Reprint of the 1980 Cognitive Science article. SHRDLU: Section "Up Through SHRDLU"; IA lending copy, full-text index. Also in the 1995 Ablex printing, archive.org/details/perspectivesonco0000unse_r2h9.

items.title: Language as a Cognitive Process, Volume 1: Syntax
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Reading, MA: Addison-Wesley. Primary work by Winograd. The syntax textbook refers back to SHRDLU as a procedural parser and as a program designed on principles of systemic grammar. SHRDLU: Several passages; IA lending copy, full-text index, including the procedural parser of SHRDLU in the ATN chapter and the systemic grammar section.

items.title: Computer Software for Working with Language
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Scientific American 251(3), September 1984. Primary work by Winograd. Winograd describes SHRDLU as an early example of conversational language programs, and says it succeeded in part because of its limited world of conversation. Reprinted in Computer Software (Scientific American book, 1985) and Language, Writing, and the Computer (1986). SHRDLU: IA OCR of the issue; the contents page lists the article at p. 90.

items.title: Driving semantics for a limited domain
items.author: Palmer, Martha Stone
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Palmer examines SHRDLU's procedural treatment of descriptive and imperative verbs and states that neither SHRDLU nor LNR has a clear method of semantic processing reflecting a theory of semantic analysis. PDF is 46 MB, recorded as a link. SHRDLU: Section 2.2.3.3 'Procedural Representation of verbs in SHRDLU', printed pp. 84-86, PDF pp. 93-95; also printed pp. 49, 97-98, 253.

items.title: Le dialogue dans une communication homme/machine
items.author: Vilnat, Anne
items.note: In: Intellectica 1(1), 1985, pp. 101-122. Calls SHRDLU the first system to pose the interesting problems of dialogue: it explained its acts and asked questions, but in a world of a dozen blocks, and citing Dreyfus 1979 its methods cannot transfer to a real universe. English gloss: Dialogue in human/machine communication. SHRDLU: printed pp. 102-104 (page text read on Persée).

items.title: What Does it Mean to Understand Language?
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Aitkenhead, A. M. and Slack, J. M. (eds), Issues in Cognitive Modeling: A Reader, chapter 8, p. 175. Primary work by Winograd. Abridged reprint of the 1980 article. SHRDLU: Chapter 8 (contents p. 175), abridged; heading "SHRDLU" in the IA full-text index. Editors from IA item metadata should be confirmed from the book.

items.title: Reference and the resolution of local syntactic ambiguity: the effect of context during human sentence processing
items.author: Altmann, Gerald T.M.
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Altmann uses Winograd's blocks-world program as the historical setting for his work on context in sentence processing and reproduces a short dialogue, showing how SHRDLU uses its world model and the preceding discourse to decide reference. SHRDLU: Chapter 3, printed pp. 59-64, PDF pp. 65-70, with a sample dialogue; further at printed pp. 76, 79, 91, 241.

items.title: Understanding Computers and Cognition: A New Foundation for Design
items.author: Winograd, Terry; Flores, Fernando
items.note: In: Norwood, NJ: Ablex. Primary work by Winograd. The authors take SHRDLU as an example of the programs they criticise, and describe its record of the conversation and its reasoning about the conversation. SHRDLU: Chapter on understanding language by computer; IA full-text index: programs of this kind, and a passage on how SHRDLU determined referents from a conversation record.

items.title: Expérience imaginaire et Intelligence Artificielle
items.author: Duyckaerts, Éric
items.note: In: Quaderni 1(1), 1987, pp. 47-63. Uses SHRDLU to illustrate AI theories as thought experiments run on a machine: a program living in a micro-world of coloured geometric objects, studied to investigate conversational English. English gloss: Imaginary experiment and artificial intelligence. SHRDLU: printed pp. 58-59, note 22 p. 63 (page text read on Persée).

items.title: In praise of wider functionalism or for more matter in mind
items.author: Edwards, James Stephen
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. A philosophy of mind thesis. Edwards sets a robot SHRDLU manipulating real blocks against T-SHRDLU, a computer manipulating another computer's block-simulation program, and argues that a wide functional system distinguishes their observation concepts where narrow functionalism does not. PDF is 47 MB, recorded as a link. SHRDLU: Abstract (PDF pp. 11-12) and the final chapter, printed pp. 265-285, PDF pp. 277-297, 67 hits; OCR damage T-SIIRDLU, SKRDLU.

items.title: Langage naturel et intelligence artificielle
items.author: Bernard, Gilles; Feat, Jym
items.note: In: Histoire Épistémologie Langage 10(1), 1988, pp. 151-170. Says Winograd implemented a systemic grammar in SHRDLU, valid only for small universes, and that in 1972 his program, with each piece of knowledge a small procedural module, set off the procedural versus declarative controversy leading to Mycin. HAL lists a copy (hal-01294596) with CC BY-ND, not seen at source because HAL's file route is behind a bot check. English gloss: Natural language and artificial intelligence. SHRDLU: printed pp. 156, 160 (page text read on Persée).

items.title: Incremental semantics and interactive syntactic processing
items.author: Haddock, N. J.
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Describes SHRDLU's blocks world, its translation of input into Planner programs and its checks against the current database as an early form of on-line reference evaluation, then criticises it for lacking an incremental semantics and for its depth-first parser. SHRDLU: Printed pp. 26-30, PDF pp. 32-36; also printed pp. 64, 130.

items.title: Traduction automatique et recherche cognitive
items.author: Villard, Masako
items.note: In: Histoire Épistémologie Langage 11(1), 1989, pp. 55-84. In a history of machine translation, says Winograd's 1971 shrdlu showed that understanding natural language required knowledge of the domain as well as of the language's internal laws. English gloss: Machine translation and cognitive research. SHRDLU: printed p. 62 (page text read on Persée).

items.title: L'Intelligence artificielle en question
items.author: Winograd, Terry; Flores, Fernando
items.note: In: Paris: Presses Universitaires de France, collection La politique éclatée. Primary work by Winograd. French translation of Understanding Computers and Cognition (1986). SHRDLU: IA lending copy, full-text index: the French text of the passage naming SHRDLU, and a preface remarking on Winograd and Paris.

items.title: Intelligence artificielle et signification. À propos des limites et des possibilitées des sciences cognitives
items.author: Mendonça, W. P.
items.note: In: Philosophiques 17(1), 1990. Snippet: SHRDLU is offered as the best example of a program operating with objects that exist only in its inner world, where properties of manipulated objects are stipulated. English gloss: Artificial intelligence and signification: on the limits and possibilities of the cognitive sciences. SHRDLU: Persée search snippet of the Érudit copy, note 10; full text on erudit.org is behind a bot check.

items.title: GRAFLOG: a theory of semantics for graphics with applications to human-computer interaction and CAD systems
items.author: Pineda Cortes, Luis Alberto
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Opens a short survey of natural language systems with SHRDLU, stating that its purpose was to show that understanding can be modelled through an integrated system. SHRDLU: Printed p. 6, PDF p. 13.

items.title: Dialogue and the machine: an interactional perspective on computer dialogue models, mediation and artifacts
items.author: McIlvenny, Paul B.
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. A paragraph presents SHRDLU as an advance on template-matching programs through its use of syntactic and semantic theories; a later passage names it with ELIZA as an implementation supporting the dialogue-partner metaphor, which the thesis criticises. PDF is 45 MB, recorded as a link. SHRDLU: PDF p. 26, and printed p. 58, PDF p. 67.

items.title: Thinking machines: Can there be? Are we?
items.author: Winograd, Terry
items.note: In: Sheehan, James J. and Sosna, Morton (eds), The Boundaries of Humanity: Humans, Animals, Machines. Berkeley: University of California Press; also Partridge, Derek and Wilks, Yorick (eds), The Foundations of Artificial Intelligence: A Sourcebook. Cambridge University Press, 1990. Primary work by Winograd. Winograd writes of his own work in AI without naming SHRDLU and argues from the phenomenological critique against symbol-system AI; the micro-world he discusses is Minsky's toy blocks of the Society of Mind. SHRDLU: The name SHRDLU does not occur in this text. Opening section: "my own understanding developed through active participation in artificial intelligence research"; Winograd cites Winograd and Flores for the argument. Free to read at https://web.archive.org/web/2005/http://hci.stanford.edu/~winograd/papers/thinking-machines.html

items.title: Focusing for Pronoun Resolution in English Discourse: An Implementation
items.author: Ersan, Ebru; Akman, Varol
items.note: In: arXiv:cmp-lg/9409005. A paragraph describes SHRDLU's arm and blocks, its pronoun handling and says that, as Winograd accepts, its rules do not suffice and its success was in many respects illusory. SHRDLU: PDF p. 13.

items.title: De la métaphore à la co-construction. Coopération intelligence artificielle/psychologie pour la conception d'une expérimentation commune
items.author: Jacquet, Denis; Nicolle, Anne; Andrès, Marc
items.note: In: Intellectica 22(1), 1996, pp. 119-144. Calls SHRDLU the first really interesting human/machine dialogue and observes that its blocks-world situations are defined by a list of formulas. English gloss: From metaphor to co-construction: AI/psychology cooperation in designing a shared experiment. SHRDLU: printed p. 122 (page text read on Persée).

items.title: SHRDLU
items.author: Flow (Everything2 user)
items.note: In: Everything2. One paragraph: the program dates from the early 1970s, by Winograd at MIT, tested theories of natural language processing and problem solving; a user typed English requests to manipulate blocks. Derives the name from ETAOIN SHRDLU. SHRDLU: The single writeup on the node (node created by user Flow, published_time 2000-07-31; writeup text read from the page's embedded data).

items.title: Grounded Semantic Composition for Visual Scenes
items.author: Gorniak, Peter; Roy, Deb
items.note: In: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 21, 429-470. A related-work paragraph compares SHRDLU's semantic interpretation during parsing with their own system, and says SHRDLU had a clean symbolic scene representation and was restricted to sentences it could parse completely. SHRDLU: section 1.2 Related Work, printed pp. 432-433, PDF pp. 4-5. Free to read at https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.0031

items.title: Как исследовать человеческое сознание эмпирически
items.author: Деннет, Дэниел
items.note: In: История философии, no. 12, 2005 (translated by Н. С. Юлина). Russian translation of Dennett, 'How to Study Human Consciousness Empirically or Nothing Comes to Mind', Synthese 53(2), 1982. Dennett crosses Shakey with Winograd's SHRDLU in a thought experiment, a hybrid that answers questions about why it moved blocks, and declines to call it a realistic model. English gloss: How to study human consciousness empirically. SHRDLU: printed p. 212, PDF p. 15; printed p. 216, PDF p. 19.
items.licence: CC BY (label "Лицензия Creative Commons" on the CyberLeninka article page)

items.title: Unmediated data-oriented generation
items.author: Cochran, Dave
items.note: In: MSc thesis, University of Edinburgh. A background section on SHRDLU as a dialogue system, placed alongside Data-Oriented Parsing and L0 as background to the author's generation model. SHRDLU: Section 2.3 'SHRDLU', printed p. 13, PDF p. 13, 9 hits.

items.title: Проблемы синтеза интеллектуального трансляционного модуля мультитранслятора для обработки речевых сообщений
items.author: Чернухин, Ю. В.; Крамарь, М. В.
items.note: In: Известия Южного федерального университета. Технические науки 77(2), thematic issue, pp. 168-169. Calls SHRDLU one of the simplest and most successful language systems, a virtual world of cubes using systemic grammar in PROGRAMMAR that coped largely because its domain was limited, then builds a SHRDLU-like noun-group grammar for robot commands. English gloss: Problems in synthesising an intelligent translation module of a multitranslator for processing speech messages. SHRDLU: printed pp. 168-169, PDF pp. 3-4, including a syntax diagram of the SHRDLU noun group (fig. 6).
items.licence: CC BY (label "Лицензия Creative Commons" on the CyberLeninka article page)

items.title: Проблемы использования многоязыковой Трансляции в контекстно-зависимых языковых средах
items.author: Чернухин, Ю. В.; Крамарь, М. В.
items.note: In: Известия Южного федерального университета. Технические науки 78(1), special issue, pp. 54-55. Describes SHRDLU's systemic grammar implemented in PROGRAMMAR and Planner, with a feature-marking parse, and compares its structure with the authors' Multitranslator environment, whose grammar language they say can implement a SHRDLU-like syntactic system, working through the noun group. English gloss: Problems of using multilanguage translation in context-dependent language environments. SHRDLU: printed pp. 54-55, PDF pp. 1-2.
items.licence: CC BY (label "Лицензия Creative Commons" on the CyberLeninka article page)

items.title: Inconsistency Robustness in Logic Programs
items.author: Hewitt, Carl
items.note: In: arXiv:0904.3036. Hewitt's account says Winograd made an impressive demo, that successors of Planner and SHRDLU could not realise procedural embedding on the hardware of the time, that Sussman and Papert spread news of SHRDLU at Edinburgh, and that the Lighthill report mentioned it favourably. SHRDLU: PDF pp. 10, 14, 15; index entry PDF p. 54.

items.title: The discipline matures: Three milestones
items.author: Bermúdez, José Luis
items.note: In: Cognitive Science: An Introduction to the Science of the Mind, Cambridge University Press, pp. 28-57. The summary presents SHRDLU as a computer model showing how grammatical rules might be represented in a cognitive system and integrated with other information about the environment, with programming built around procedures for specialised tasks. SHRDLU: Chapter 2, section 2.1, per the chapter summary on the publisher's page; full chapter behind access control.

items.title: The Stupidity of Computers
items.author: Auerbach, David
items.note: In: n+1, issue 13 (Machine Politics), Winter 2012. Presents SHRDLU as following ELIZA, reproduces a stretch of dialogue, says sentences had to be turned into a logical syntax, and places its success in the very narrow domain of colored blocks. SHRDLU: Section on Eliza and Shrdlu, about 400 words, with a transcript of the dialogue.

items.title: Dead Media Beat: Early Artificial Intelligence Projects
items.author: Sterling, Bruce
items.note: In: WIRED (Beyond the Beyond blog). A chronological list of early AI projects reproduced by Sterling; SHRDLU is one dated line. SHRDLU: List entry under 1970.

items.title: Building the Second Mind, 1961-1980: From the Ascendancy of ARPA to the Advent of Commercial Expert Systems
items.author: Skinner, Rebecca E.
items.note: In: Self-published beta edition, ISBN 978-0-9894543-2-2; deposited in eScholarship, UC Berkeley Previously Published Works, 2012-09-03. A history of ARPA-era AI that places SHRDLU among the MIT microworld dissertations and treats it and Shakey as impressive demonstrations with a 'wow' factor by the early 1970s. SHRDLU: PDF pp. 12, 215, 231-235, 249, 335 (18 occurrences).

items.title: SHRDLU
items.author: Hacker News contributors
items.note: In: Hacker News, item 8219409 (19 comments). Comments on closed-world assumptions and non-monotonic reasoning as reasons such systems are not in use, and on the link from the dissertation's ambiguity discussion (p. 290) to the Winograd Schema. SHRDLU: Whole thread, read through the Algolia API.

items.title: SHRDLU, understanding, anthropomorphisation and hindsight bias
items.author: Stuart_Armstrong
items.note: In: LessWrong. Reproduces part of the dialogue and argues that belief in SHRDLU was not unreasonable at the time, since the approach's failure in general situations was not yet known. SHRDLU: Whole post (read on the greaterwrong.com viewer).

items.title: AI's Language Problem
items.author: Knight, Will
items.note: In: MIT Technology Review. Recounts Winograd building the block world and SHRDLU at MIT from 1968, how it parsed typed commands and tracked reference. Says it was seen as progress but was an illusion: enlarging the world made the rules unmanageable, and Winograd left AI. SHRDLU: Section on Winograd, several paragraphs.

items.title: Learning Executable Semantic Parsers for Natural Language Understanding
items.author: Liang, Percy
items.note: In: arXiv:1603.06677; Communications of the ACM 59(9), 2016. Opens with SHRDLU and LUNAR as early systems that integrated syntax, semantics and reasoning, quoting a blocks world query SHRDLU could process, then says hand-crafted rules did not generalise. SHRDLU: PDF p. 1.

items.title: Conversational AI and the road ahead
items.author: Bailey, Katherine
items.note: In: TechCrunch. Describes SHRDLU as an early conversational system restricted to statements and questions about blocks, and says conversational AI products still need such restrictions. SHRDLU: Late section on restricted domains, one sentence and a figure caption.

items.title: Siri, Who Is Terry Winograd?
items.author: Fisher, Lawrence M.
items.note: In: strategy+business. Profile of Winograd. Reproduces the opening of the dialogue, gives the ETAOIN SHRDLU source of the name, and reports the backlash, quoting Ben Shneiderman that SHRDLU had the illusion of broader capabilities but was restricted to a few words and concepts. SHRDLU: Middle section of the profile, several paragraphs.

items.title: SHRDLU (1971)
items.author: Hacker News contributors
items.note: In: Hacker News, item 14351485 (30 comments). Comments on memories of the program, why it did not scale, and lambda calculus in later semantic analysis. SHRDLU: Whole thread, read through the Algolia API.

items.title: Syntax-mediated semantic parsing
items.author: Reddy Goli, Venkata Sivakumar
items.note: In: PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. Names LUNAR and SHRDLU as the two systems behind the early success of semantic parsing and gives a paragraph on SHRDLU's use of context, its clarification questions and its rule-based semantic component. SHRDLU: Introduction, printed p. 2 and following, PDF pp. 17-18.

items.title: Is artificial intelligence going off the rails?
items.author: Timms, Aaron
items.note: In: The Outline. One paragraph: the program made Winograd a star in AI, and during the 1970s he began to question the field's approach. Says the name was an inside joke drawn from Mad magazine. SHRDLU: One paragraph in the middle of the article.

items.title: "эпистемологический поворот" как условие философской концептуализации когнитивной науки (к 85-летию акад. В. А. Лекторского)
items.author: Бакулов, Виктор Дмитриевич; Силенко, Светлана Владимировна
items.note: In: Научная мысль Кавказа, 2017 no. 4 (92). Presents SHRDLU as a step toward reproducing human speech and understanding in programs, showing interaction through grammatical structures with visualisation; it lacks social communication but raised the question of language algorithms for coding meaning. English gloss: The 'epistemological turn' as a condition of the philosophical conceptualisation of cognitive science. SHRDLU: printed p. 23, PDF p. 3.
items.licence: CC BY (label "Лицензия Creative Commons" on the CyberLeninka article page)

items.title: Photo-Realistic Blocksworld Dataset
items.author: Asai, Masataro
items.note: In: arXiv:1812.01818. Traces the Blocksworld domain to SHRDLU, says SHRDLU heavily inspires the CLEVR benchmark, reproduces an image from Winograd's work and notes the original environment contained unstackable pyramids. SHRDLU: section 2, The Blocksworld Domain, PDF p. 2; Figure 3 reproduces the SHRDLU display, PDF p. 4; PDF p. 5.

items.title: Getting Beyond the Toy Domain. Meditations on David Deamer’s “Assembling Life”
items.author: Bains, W.
items.note: In: Life (Basel). Describes SHRDLU planning block movements from English instructions and says its methods could not be extended to requests such as moving objects round a kitchen. Uses this as an analogy for origin-of-life research. SHRDLU: Section using SHRDLU and Blocks World as the example of a toy domain; named again later in the comparison with origin-of-life experiments (Europe PMC full-text XML).

items.title: How SHRDLU got its name (2003)
items.author: Hacker News contributors
